pull_requests.title: Grid Core Orthogonal Coordinate Authority
pull_requests.goal: Make grid_core satisfy its public orthogonal-lattice semantics without weakening the held-out structural test.
scope: Create one shared x-coordinate authority for grid_core across all rows.
Keep deterministic spacing variability along each axis without creating diagonal semantic vertical roads.
Preserve exact-mm topology, road hierarchy, outer mainline/ramp grammar, DCEL construction, and replay.
Convert held-out seeds 503, 701, and 907 into explicit regression fixtures.
out_of_scope: Changing public grid_core semantics to permit diagonals.
red: Add parameterized regression over seeds 503, 701, and 907.
Add a seed-differentiation test proving different seeds can change spacing while preserving orthogonality.
green: Refactor grid_core to construct one shared x axis before row construction.
Connect adjacent rows by identical x-coordinate identity instead of monotone partial matching.
Keep horizontal roads on exact y constants and vertical roads on exact x constants.
steps: Trace all grid_core callers and ensure no downstream code relies on row-local x-coordinate counts.
Introduce a shared x-axis variable for grid_core using deterministic seed/style/scale inputs.
Use exact coordinate equality for vertical road endpoints.
Re-run topology/DCEL/static-authority tests and held-out regression tests.
Regenerate only artifacts whose bytes are legitimately changed; do not rewrite the frozen 2026-08-23 audit evidence.
acceptance: For seeds 503, 701, and 907, every semantic surface-horizontal road is exactly horizontal.
For seeds 503, 701, and 907, every semantic surface-vertical road is exactly vertical.
grid_core remains one connected surface fabric except intentionally separated non-surface layers.
No same-layer proper crossing or unregistered touch is introduced.
DCEL area conservation and deterministic replay remain unchanged.
No threshold is weakened and no held-out result is reclassified as fresh holdout evidence.

claim.allowed: grid_core implements an exact orthogonal coordinate lattice in the exercised regression seeds
claim.not_allowed: grid_core is empirically realistic or traffic-optimal

stop: The shared-axis change breaks exact topology or DCEL invariants and cannot be repaired locally.
A dependency on row-local axes is discovered outside grid_core; document it before expanding scope.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-001 only. Read AGENTS.md and the 2026-08-23 held-out audit first.
Use behavior-cluster TDD. Do not relax the grid_core structural contract.
Demonstrate RED on the current row-local-axis implementation, then introduce one
exact shared x-axis authority for grid_core. Preserve mm coordinates, deterministic
replay, multilayer topology, DCEL, static authority, and public style IDs. Treat
seeds 503/701/907 as regression data, not as a new holdout. Do not touch CAPR,
traffic routing, security, branch protection, or unrelated assurance machinery.
Produce one focused commit and a concise verification receipt.

pull_requests.title: Style Capability and Public Claim SSOT
pull_requests.goal: Make every public style name, compatibility ID, implemented mechanism, unsupported combination, and claim ceiling derive from one typed capability registry.
scope: Add a typed style capability registry owned by the city-generation package.
Record public label, compatibility ID, implemented structural claims, explicitly unclaimed functions, and supported generator arms.
Make gallery labels, benchmark preclassification, and config validation consume the registry.
Replace free-form skip reason strings with an enum or closed typed code set.
red: Add a test proving gallery labels and generator capability labels come from the same registry.
Add a test proving unknown style IDs and unknown skip reason codes fail closed.
Add a test proving standard supported styles equal the generator-exported capability set.
green: Route generator, benchmark, config, and gallery queries through the registry.
steps: Define the minimal registry; do not introduce plugin or framework machinery.
Encode organic as curvilinear warped grid, not organic topology.
Encode polycentric_tod and superblock_mixed structural claims separately from traffic-functional claims.
Use enum reason codes in structured skip artifacts.
Update only claim prose directly affected by the registry.
acceptance: There is exactly one source of truth for style IDs, labels, supported arms, and claim ceilings.
Unknown style and skip codes are rejected.
No geometry, fingerprint, or runtime-default behavior changes.
Existing artifacts reproduce unless their label or structured reason field is intentionally versioned.

claim.allowed: public style labels are bounded by implemented structural mechanisms
claim.not_allowed: style labels imply empirical or traffic validity

stop: The registry begins duplicating configuration or becoming a generic plugin framework.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-002 after MAP-PR-001 is merged. Build a minimal frozen style
capability registry and a closed SkipReason type. Make generator support queries,
config validation, gallery labels, and morphology-control-table preclassification
consume it. Preserve geometry and fingerprints unless a public label or structured
skip representation is intentionally versioned. Do not add a plugin system or a
generic governance framework. Keep structural and traffic-functional claims separate.

pull_requests.title: Deterministic Correlated Development Field V2
pull_requests.goal: Replace cellwise hash noise used as a spatial-development proxy with a deterministic field that has explicit correlation lengths and units for non-grid styles.
scope: Introduce a versioned deterministic multiscale correlated field.
Expose correlation length, amplitude, and unit-bearing parameters.
Use the field only for styles whose contract allows curvilinear or heterogeneous growth.
Keep grid_core on its exact orthogonal coordinate authority.
Preserve reproducibility across tile order and process order.
out_of_scope: Full elevation, hydrology, or land-market simulation.
red: Add exact replay tests for value and gradient queries.
Add a spatial autocorrelation test over a fixed lattice.
Add a negative test proving adjacent samples are not independent hash noise.
green: Implement deterministic multi-octave value/gradient noise or another explicitly documented correlated construction.
Quantize/canonicalize inputs and outputs enough to preserve supported replay targets.
Wire the field into non-grid styles only.
steps: Choose one small mathematical construction and document units.
Keep all parameters in a frozen config and fingerprint.
Avoid external libraries unless already required.
Re-render style diagnostics and inspect for foldovers/crossings.
Record negative results if correlation creates topology failures.
acceptance: Fixed seed and coordinates reproduce bit-identically on the supported Python environment.
Tile traversal order does not change generated topology.
Measured correlation at short separation exceeds correlation at long separation on a fixed test lattice.
grid_core geometry and fingerprints remain unchanged.
No proper same-layer crossing or unregistered touch is introduced.

claim.allowed: non-grid styles use a deterministic spatially correlated development field
claim.not_allowed: the field is calibrated terrain or real urban development

stop: The implementation requires a large generic noise framework.
Topology invariants cannot be maintained without broad repair heuristics.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-003 only. Introduce a compact deterministic correlated
development field with explicit metre-scale correlation parameters and a
stable fingerprint. Use it for non-grid styles while leaving grid_core exact
and unchanged. TDD must include replay, tile-order independence, and measured
autocorrelation. Do not learn from OSM or add a full terrain simulator. If
the field causes crossings or non-determinism, stop and preserve the negative
result rather than adding broad post-hoc repair.

pull_requests.title: Directed Interchange and Ramp Grammar
pull_requests.goal: Give ramps and interchanges explicit directional merge/diverge semantics instead of treating one connector as a bidirectional road.
scope: Represent ON_RAMP and OFF_RAMP behavior, or equivalent one-way access contracts.
Create legal merge/diverge movement records.
Reject at-grade surface/mainline crossing without typed interchange or layer separation.
Preserve deterministic gateway placement and physical road identities.
out_of_scope: CAPR, neural routing, or demand calibration.
red: Add tests that an on-ramp admits surface-to-mainline but not mainline-to-surface movement.
Add test rejecting a flat mainline/surface intersection with no interchange.
Add runtime route-legality tests through each interchange direction.
green: Split or type ramp connectors by direction.
Emit exact legal movements at merge/diverge nodes.
Preserve physical layer crossings without accidental junctions.
steps: Choose the minimum schema change compatible with existing graph contracts.
Migrate generated scalable maps only; keep historical import behavior versioned.
Ensure physical-road and directed-link fingerprints reflect the new semantics.
Re-run route construction and static-authority integration tests.
acceptance: Every generated ramp has an explicit directional purpose.
No illegal reverse ramp movement is present.
Every mainline access gateway has at least one legal entry and one legal exit path, possibly via separate ramps.
No at-grade mainline/surface junction is silently created.
Replay and conservation tests remain green.

claim.allowed: generated interchanges have typed directional ramp semantics

stop: The change requires lane-level simulation or broad runtime rewrite.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-004 after MAP-PR-003. Add the smallest explicit directional
interchange contract that distinguishes on-ramps, off-ramps, merges, and
diverges. TDD must prove legal and illegal movements. Preserve multilayer
geometry and deterministic identities. Do not expand into lane-changing,
signals, CAPR, or generic motorway simulation.

pull_requests.title: Scale-Aware Infrastructure Budgets
pull_requests.goal: Make gateway, ring, centre, bridge, and hierarchy budgets explicit deterministic functions of city scale and barrier geometry.
scope: Define bounded formulas for infrastructure counts/spacing as functions of area and style.
Keep population separate from topology unless a future model explicitly changes that contract.
Test 25, 40, 100, and 250 km².
Preserve deterministic topology under tile order changes.
red: Add monotonicity and boundedness tests across 25/40/100/250 km².
Add style-specific minimum-connectivity tests at each scale.
Add deterministic replay and tile-order tests.
green: Implement explicit integer budget formulas with documented rounding.
Route all infrastructure counts through one budget object.
steps: Measure current counts/densities before choosing formulas.
Use simple piecewise or square-root area scaling; avoid fitted black boxes.
Bind formulas and results to the topology fingerprint.
Re-run memory/time measurements but do not introduce performance thresholds before observing them.
acceptance: Budget outputs are deterministic, bounded, and monotone where physically intended.
All four scales produce connected core surface networks.
river_constrained retains at least two failure-independent cross-bank paths at scales where the barrier spans the city.
ring_radial and polycentric_tod do not collapse to one fixed-size motif surrounded by empty area.
road-length density remains finite and reported in km/km².

claim.allowed: infrastructure counts follow an explicit multiscale contract
claim.not_allowed: the scale formulas are empirically calibrated

stop: Budget formulas become dependent on unmeasured empirical constants or hidden tuning.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-005 only. First measure current 25/40/100/250 km² counts,
then introduce a small deterministic InfrastructureBudget object with explicit
units and rounding. Preserve the documented separation between area-driven
geometry and population-driven demand. Do not fit external data or freeze
performance thresholds before measurement.
